partners.mechanism_chain: ERCC1 (HGNC:3090) —DISRUPTS→ Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) (GO:0006289); Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) (GO:0006289) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebrooculofacioskeletal syndrome (HP:0001288); XPA (HGNC:12044) —DISRUPTS→ Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) (GO:0006289); Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) (GO:0006289) —LEADS_TO→ Extreme photosensitivity (HP:0000971); Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) (GO:0006289) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263). Mutations in ERCC1 (for disease A, Cockayne Syndrome) and XPA (for disease B, Xeroderma Pigmentosum group A) both disrupt the Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) pathway. Impairment of NER leads to the accumulation of unrepaired DNA damage, which in turn causes a spectrum of phenotypes. For ERCC1 deficiency, this can manifest as Cerebrooculofacioskeletal syndrome (a feature of severe Cockayne Syndrome). For XPA deficiency, the primary consequence is extreme photosensitivity, a hallmark of Xeroderma Pigmentosum, and also developmental delay.
